submitter: bugs_open/395 session — routing rule 3b: a finding is not routed at a handler that cannot WRITE the field its own acceptance criterion names
rationale: bugs_open/395 filed that an item closes `complete` while its own stated acceptance test is unmet. Completion gate 1c (69479bcf6, council 064841bd, live on v1.0.1339) DETECTS that. This change addresses the cause it detects, and the cause is not what 395 originally said. [MEASURED 2026-08-25, live DB + first-hand code reads] all three acceptance predicates ever emitted grade `pages.meta_description`, and all three are routed at `page-build-handler`, which has NO step that can write that column. Every writer of the column is create-or-fill-blank (site_db_actions.go:1235 and apply_adoption_plan_action.go:84 are both COALESCE(NULLIF(EXCLUDED,''), existing)) except save_page_meta_description_action.go:211, reachable from exactly one live agent whose scheduled pre_query selects COALESCE(meta_description,'')='' — empty values only. So the handler could not have satisfied the criterion whatever it was told: the item was routed at an agent structurally incapable of the work, it rebuilt and deployed the page truthfully, and the estate recorded a green completion for something impossible. This is NOT new: bugs_open/320 §5 measured the same page, same field, same handler, same outcome on 2026-08-19, and its §9 says in terms 'Do not file content_rewrite items for them'. A different producer broke that rule on 2026-08-24. Neither lane was careless — §9 is prose in a bug file and NOTHING ENFORCES PROSE. That is the framework defect this change fixes: it is 320 §9 with an enforcer attached. Scope is deliberately narrow and the limit is stated rather than buried: it fires only where a finding names its field MECHANICALLY (a CLM-024 predicate); prose-only acceptance tests are undecidable at this seam and pass through untouched. The complementary half — stamping the same verdict at emission so the predicate carries it — is owned by the vigilant_designer_offer_analysis lane and calls the SAME exported helper, agreed in writing today, so there is one answer to 'can this handler write this field' rather than two that drift.

plan.summary: Wrap classifyFinding with a capability guard: a finding whose acceptance predicate names a page field the routed handler cannot write becomes a capability_gap (the shape Rule 3 already uses for noHandlerCategories) instead of dispatchable work. Opt-in per field, roster carries its measurement and date, one exported helper shared with the emit gate.
plan.risks: The roster is a NEGATIVE capability claim and goes stale BY ADDITION: the day page-build-handler gains a meta_description step, the roster keeps parking findings that have become fixable. That is the SAFE direction (it parks loudly on a read surface rather than filing a doomed item) but it is still wrong, so every entry carries a Measured date and the `git log --since` re-check, per the 2026-08-22 counting ruling. A live-drift audit in the WII-031 shape is the named follow-on, not built here. It converts work items that today are dispatchable. Measured blast radius: only findings carrying a CLM-024 predicate over meta_description/title can be affected, which is 3 rows all-history, all already terminal — so no in-flight work changes hands. Prose-only findings (the other ~6,900) are untouched by construction and there is a negative-control test for exactly that. capability_gap is not a bin: [MEASURED 2026-08-25] 50 existing rows and TWO readers (diagnose_triage_action.go:361, fixloop_digest_action.go:358, both `WHERE item_type='capability_gap' OR status='deferred'`), so a parked finding lands somewhere already looked at. If those readers ever go away this becomes silence, which is what bugs_open/320 was filed about. The guard reads the REJECTED predicate as well as the live one. If it did not, the emit-side half and this half would blind each other: theirs fires first, the field disappears from where this one looks, and both report success. That ordering hazard is the reason for the shared helper and is pinned by a test.
grounded_in: bugs_open/320 §5: 'filing content_rewrite items is not a workaround — it is the expensive version of doing nothing, and it leaves a green record saying the opposite.'
bugs_open/320 §9: 'Do not file content_rewrite items for them. §5: measured, completes, does nothing.'
bugs_open/320 §4: 'No UPDATE path exists. All seven writers of the column are create-or-upsert.' and 'ask who owns the field first.'

bugs_open/395 §9 (written by the owning lane after verifying this finding first-hand): 'the handler could not have satisfied the criterion whatever it was told. §6's negative control is not merely missing — it is UNREACHABLE.'

verify_acceptance_predicates_action.go:277-281 — AcceptancePredicateRejection is {Verdict, Reason, Predicate}, so a rejected predicate's `field` is one level down; reading ['field'] off the wrapper silently yields ''.

edits.rationale: The roster, the exported helper and the guard, in one new file rather than as branches inside the 1000-line router — so the diff is reviewable and the router's own edit is one line. The roster is opt-in per FIELD with the zero value meaning 'not measured', following acceptancePredicateGates/noChangeGates: absent from the map means route exactly as before, so an unmeasured field can never be treated as either capability or incapacity.

Rename the existing router body to classifyFindingRoute and make classifyFinding a wrapper that applies the guard. It is a WRAPPER and not a branch inside the router deliberately: the router decides the handler in several independent places (Rule 3, Rule 4, the category table), so a branch would be bypassed by any route added later. Wrapping makes the guard total over routes that do not exist yet — the difference between making the bad state unrepresentable and merely absent today. One production call site (line ~1006) and nine test call sites keep working unchanged.

Five tests, each written so that deleting the thing it guards makes it FAIL, and all three mutations were RUN and observed failing rather than asserted: (1) remove the guard call -> the worked case routes at page-build-handler again, FAILED as required; (2) drop the nested-predicate unwrapping -> predicateTargetField returns "" and the guard goes silently inert, FAILED as required; (3) add a third field to acceptancePredicateTextFields -> the vocabulary lockstep FAILED as required. Plus a negative control (a prose-only finding must route UNCHANGED — a guard that converts everything is indistinguishable from one that works) and a roster test requiring every entry to carry [MEASURED ...] and a date.
